verdicts.reasoning: The diff hand-builds a modal with a native <dialog> element (showModal/close) and inline styles. It imports only Alert and Button from @acme/ds and does not use any design-system dialog or confirmation component. The API reference provided lists no dialog component, and the diff never shows one being used. This is not clearly the design system's confirmation pattern, so it cannot be marked as passing. It is also more than a bare inline warning, since it does use a modal overlay.

Inside the dialog, the 'Delete account' button uses variant="destructive" and is disabled until the 'I understand' checkbox is checked. The 'Cancel' button is variant="secondary" and carries data-initial-focus, so focus lands on the safe action when the dialog opens. The destructive action is visually distinct and is neither default-focused nor the primary action.

A visible Cancel button calls onCancel, and Escape is routed through the dialog's onCancel handler to the same cancel path, so the user can exit at any time. The copy states the consequence plainly: 'This can't be undone', 'Your profile, projects and settings will be permanently deleted. We can't restore them afterwards.' The outer section also says 'Permanently delete your account... This can't be undone.' The extra checkbox adds friction but does not block backing out.
